title: resolvers
description: Named reads of the trigger kind's context. A data graph or a binding uses a resolver under its reads as @path#name and reads it as {{name}} or {{name.field}}, and the value comes straight from request.* -- nothing runs. This is the one place a feature says what it takes from the request; a domain graph never reads it. Lives in a feature's edge/ directory, since request.* is the world's vocabulary.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/resolvers.schema.json.

description.description: What these resolvers read, in one or two sentences.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

resolvers.description: name -> what it reads. The name is what a graph or a binding uses under reads as @path#name, and reads as {{name}}.

read.description: A path into the request, from the root request: request.params.id, request.body.title, request.headers['user-agent']. A key that is not an identifier is written in brackets and quotes.

label.description: A short human name for this resolver, shown instead of its name.

description.description: What this resolver reads, for a reader of the document that uses it as {{name}}.

required.description: true: the value is read as present, so it may feed a required input. Every trigger whose run reaches this read must then guarantee it: its kind hands the path always, or one of its policies lists it under proves (A006). What a policy proves is what the guard hands once the caller is identified: request.principal, request.session.
